A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SFBD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching v1’s Appendices A–E to v2 and identifying the added Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and CelebA experiments, including SFBD FIDs, clean-data and noise-level ablations, transfer experiments and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds comparator results, quantitative denoising evaluations and memorization analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains clean-data pretraining followed by alternating backward sampling and denoiser updates. The objectives, architecture and sampling procedure are unchanged. The newly explicit single-corrupted-copy description does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10 and CelebA, Gaussian corruption, clean-subset pretraining and CIFAR class-transfer scenarios. The added denoising and memorization analyses examine this existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds TweedieDiff+ to the generative comparisons and Restormer to a new quantitative denoising comparison. It removes AmbDiff from Table 1, although AmbDiff’s qualitative examples remain in Figure 2. The stronger TweedieDiff+ comparator materially changes the competitive assessment.

E3.justification: v2 introduces FID evaluation of intermediate denoised datasets across iterations and a DINOv2 nearest-neighbor similarity protocol using 50,000 generated images, including a clean-trained control. Figure 1 also reports a 10%-clean, noise-0.2 configuration. Existing generation-FID procedures, splits and Appendix E settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original ablations remain. New analyses test noise-dependent memorization through similarity distributions and matching image pairs in Appendix F, and compare iterative SFBD denoising with Restormer in Table 2. The CelebA case study also replaces the glasses example with a microphone-to-goatee example.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. Appendix F’s new histograms describe image similarities, not uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: New Figure 1 reports TweedieDiff+/SFBD FIDs of 8.05/13.53 with 50 clean images at noise 0.2, 2.81/2.58 with 10% clean at noise 0.2, and 6.75/6.31 with 4% clean at noise 0.59. Table 2 and Appendix F add denoising and similarity results; AmbDiff’s 114.13 entry disappears from Table 1. Previously reported SFBD benchmark values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds Fourier-decay reasoning and smooth, bounded-support assumptions to argue that characteristic-function comparisons can be restricted to a compact frequency domain. It also corrects score-function expressions in the proof. The existing theorem statements and Proposition 2 convergence bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about deconvolution difficulty, clean pretraining, SFBD convergence and headline CIFAR-10 FIDs. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes poorer performance with very little clean data to possible pretraining overfitting, distinguishes distribution matching from exact image reconstruction, and explicitly excludes clean pretraining samples from privacy protection. It also adds interpretations of memorization tests and a quality–leakage tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 adds an SFBD code-repository link, documents the DINOv2 similarity calculation, and explicitly states that each sensitive example has one fixed corrupted version throughout training. Appendix E’s architecture, optimizer, sampling and dataset-processing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work gains focused comparisons with Daras et al. (2025), public-data-assisted private estimation and DiffPure. References supporting the new Fourier discussion, DINOv2 analysis and Restormer comparison are added. The overall deconvolution-based research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the abstract and performance discussion, expands explanations, and adds Appendix F, acknowledgements and affiliation/publication information. The original section sequence and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a comparison bar chart, a denoising table, a similarity histogram and three image-pair displays. It replaces the second CelebA case-study row and relocates retained displays. The original Appendix D sample grids are preserved rather than newly generated visual content.

improvement.justification: The stronger baseline comparison, explicit memorization diagnostics and code-access information improve empirical scrutiny and reproducibility documentation. However, new interpretations overreach: Table 2 reports first-iteration CelebA FIDs of 47.69 for SFBD versus 18.90 for Restormer, contradicting the blanket advantage claimed in the prose. Appendix F’s similarity checks also do not establish a general privacy guarantee. These limitations temper the gains.
